sources.title: E. Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Living Reviews in Relativity 22 (2019), article 3 (DOI 10.1007/s41114-019-0019-x), 202 PDF pages

contents.name: Definition 2.3 and Theorem 2.4: strictly convex normal neighborhoods and the joint exponential diffeomorphism
contents.support: The existence theorem restates that coordinate balls can be chosen strictly convex normal with the unique contained joining segment and the position vector; the joint exponential smoothness is proved locally in lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism.

contents.name: Section 2.2: local causality inside a normal neighborhood, the exponential cone and the displacement-length bound
contents.support: The theorem proves that causal reachability inside a convex normal ball is the exponential cone, that the Lorentzian length is bounded by the displacement radius and that null endpoints force the null geodesic, with supporting lemmas on the position-vector differential and length monotonicity.

contents.name: Theorem 2.12 and Definition 2.16: locally Lipschitz parametrization of continuous causal curves and inextendibility
contents.support: The lemma proves the equivalence of the absolutely continuous and continuous causal conventions and constructs one-sided inextendible extensions; no equivalence with the literature's lettering is imported.

contents.name: Section 2.11: limit curve theorems (Theorems 2.53 and 2.69)
contents.support: The basic limit curve lemma supplies causal limit curves on compact parameter intervals and future-inextendible half-line limits from h-arclength parametrized families.

contents.name: Section 2.11: the two-endpoint limit curve alternative for bounded and unbounded auxiliary lengths
contents.support: The theorem proves the bounded/unbounded alternative with the reverse-pair closure relation, which is what the Cauchy-to-global-hyperbolicity deduction and the compact cone lemma consume.

contents.name: Sections 2.14-2.15: achronal and acausal sets, achronal boundaries as local Lipschitz graphs
contents.support: The lemma proves that achronal boundaries in a globally hyperbolic manifold are locally Lipschitz graphs, topological hypersurfaces and null for the smooth volume density, using local cone bounds.

contents.name: Theorem 2.37 and Theorem 2.41: length as a limit of sums of local time separations and upper semicontinuity under uniform convergence
contents.support: The theorem proves the refined-sum formula from continuously varying local separations and the upper semicontinuity of the Lorentzian length under uniform convergence, with the full local convexity inputs.

contents.name: Section 1.6 with Theorem 1.5 (Nomizu-Ozeki: a complete Riemannian metric in every conformal class) and the Hopf-Rinow compactness of closed balls, printed pp. 10-11; Definition 2.16 and Lemma 2.17 on unbounded h-arclength, printed pp. 33-34
contents.support: The auxiliary metric construction and its completeness are exactly the conformal-class completion of section 1.6, and the closed-bounded-compact property is the Hopf-Rinow equivalence recorded there; Lemma 2.17 supplies the unbounded-arclength companion used by the limit-curve arguments.

contents.name: Definition 1.34 and sections 4.2-4.5, Definition 4.117 and Theorem 4.119: strong causality, compact causal diamonds and the equivalence with the Cauchy-set property
contents.support: The theorem proves that a Cauchy set forces strong causality and compact causal diamonds, and the converse structural facts are proved in lem-gr-globally-hyperbolic-causal-structure; no equivalent formulation is assumed.

contents.name: Theorem 4.119 and the volume-function proof (continuous strictly increasing time function with Cauchy levels)
contents.support: The volume time function, its continuity and strict monotonicity and the Cauchy property of every level are proved from the finite smooth volume density and the chronological volume continuity lemma.

contents.name: Section 4.5, Theorem 4.120: smooth temporal functions with Cauchy levels
contents.support: The theorem constructs the smooth temporal function from locally finite sums of weak steps, proves the Cauchy property of its levels and supplies the complete orthogonal flow, with every intermediate lemma authored locally.

contents.name: Section 3.1-3.3: domains of dependence, Cauchy horizons and global properties of Cauchy sets
contents.support: From the Cauchy-set property the lemma proves closedness, the past-set/set/future-set splitting and the locally Lipschitz graph property, which is the part of the domain theory the splitting consumes.

contents.name: Domains of dependence and Cauchy horizon calculus for arbitrary sets
contents.reason: The page defines the domain of dependence and the Cauchy horizon on the earlier causal-boundaries page and uses neither them nor their calculus; building them here would duplicate an existing published supplier.

contents.name: Section 2.2, pp. 26-27: strictly convex normal neighborhoods and the convexity argument of Theorem 2.4 (small coordinate balls and the local two-point geometry)
contents.support: The local containment and speed estimates for geodesics in a small ball are the quantitative reading of the convexity argument of Theorem 2.4; the item proves the explicit constants from the coordinate geodesic equation.

sources.title: P. T. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706 (2011), lecture notes with complete proofs
sources.locator: Sections 2.2.1-2.2.3, 2.4, 2.9 and 2.11; Proposition 2.2.3, Definition 2.2.7, Lemma 2.4.14, Corollary 2.4.19, Theorem 2.9.9, Lemma 2.9.11, Theorem 2.11.1, Lemmas 2.11.2-2.11.3; printed pp. 8-13, 26-28, 46-50 and 57-60

contents.name: Proposition 2.2.3 and Definition 2.2.7: time functions, causality conditions and closed causal curves
contents.support: The openness of the chronological relation and closedness of future and past sets are proved locally; the foundational vocabulary itself is supplied by the earlier physics page.

contents.name: Lemma 2.4.14 and Corollary 2.4.19: limit curves under auxiliary-length control
contents.support: The two-endpoint alternative is proved with the same bounded/unbounded-length split and the closure relation between the two limit ends.

contents.name: Theorem 2.9.9 and Lemma 2.9.11: global hyperbolicity, compact causal diamonds and the closedness of the causal relation
contents.support: The closure of the causal relation and compactness of truncated cones over compact sets are proved from compact diamonds and strong causality.

contents.name: Theorem 2.11.1 with Lemmas 2.11.2-2.11.3: the volume function, its continuity, strict monotonicity and limits along inextendible causal curves
contents.support: The volume-time proof is followed exactly: finite smooth density, almost-everywhere convergence of the chronological indicators, continuity from above and divergence along causal curves.

contents.name: The cone-bump smoothing and locally finite shell sum in the proof of Theorem 2.11.1
contents.support: The weak step is constructed from locally finite cone bumps and a negative plateau; the forward/backward step ratio and its causal-or-zero gradient are proved locally.

contents.name: The derivative-controlled strip series of the temporal-function proof
contents.support: The strip function is produced by finitely averaging weak steps over a compact slice and summing the resulting functions with rapidly decaying derivative-controlled coefficients.

contents.name: Complete smooth temporal splitting with orthogonal flow
contents.support: The paired strip series, the completeness of the gradient flow and the orthogonal product form are proved with the manifold escape lemma and the flow theory of the library.

contents.name: Sections 2.2-2.3: normal coordinates, Proposition 2.2.6 with proof (printed pp. 12-13, geodesic convexity of small coordinate balls), Definition 2.2.7 (elementary regions)
contents.support: The normal-coordinate construction, the second-derivative estimate f′′ ≥ 0 for small coordinate balls, and the elementary-region notion are given with complete proofs and are the local-geometry layer of the strictly convex normal neighborhood theorem.

contents.name: Incompleteness, singularity theorems and maximality statements
contents.reason: The page is a local and global causal-structure development feeding the GR14 and GR15 analyses; geodesic incompleteness and singularity conclusions are not part of its assigned inventory.

contents.name: Proposition 2.2.6 with proof (printed pp. 12-13): geodesic convexity of small coordinate balls and the estimate |Σ(xμ−x₀μ)Γμαβ dxα/ds dxβ/ds| ≤ C r₀ Σ(dxμ/ds)²
contents.support: The proof of the second-derivative inequality for the squared coordinate radius along a geodesic is the convexity kernel of the item; the coordinate-ball convexity conclusion is stated and proved there in the same chart geometry used by the batch.

contents.name: Proposition 2.2.6 proof: the second-derivative estimate controlling a geodesic in a small coordinate ball by its initial velocity
contents.support: The differential inequality obtained in the proof is the local speed control from which the item derives its explicit two-sided constants.

contents.name: Global smooth temporal function with Cauchy levels on a globally hyperbolic spacetime
contents.support: The statement and proof route are matched clause by clause; the construction here is the scaffold-based volume-time-plus-step-series proof, with every lemma authored locally.

contents.name: Orthogonal splitting by the complete flow of the temporal gradient
contents.support: The diffeomorphism onto the product with the level space, the absence of mixed terms and the positivity of the level metric reproduce the source's splitting conclusion.

contents.name: Application of the splitting to the existence of Cauchy hypersurfaces
contents.support: The local Cauchy neighborhood lemma supplies the local half of the Cauchy-surface implication used with the global splitting on the same page.

contents.name: Step averaging over compact slices and the derivative-controlled series
contents.support: The finite averaging of weak steps and the rapidly decaying coefficient series with uniform derivative control is exactly the construction of the strip lemma.

contents.name: Level-set control along the constructed temporal function
contents.support: The volume function supplies the continuous Cauchy levels that carry the construction; smoothness is only claimed for the final temporal function, as in the source.

contents.name: Smoothability of arbitrary Cauchy hypersurfaces
contents.reason: This page constructs its own smooth temporal function from the volume time; smoothing a prescribed Cauchy hypersurface is not among the assigned claims and would need the space-time splitting theory.

alternatives.argument: The convexity statement is proved in the item from the coordinate geodesic equation: for f(s):=|x(γ(s))|²_e one has f″=2|ẋ|²_e−2x·Γ(x)[ẋ,ẋ]≥0 on a small coordinate ball, hence no interior maximum for f. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706, Proposition 2.2.6 with complete proof (pp. 12-13) proves the same statement from the same displayed estimate, and Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Theorem 2.4 (p. 26-27) states the coordinate-ball form of strict convexity; both sources are fetch-verified in this coverage file.

The two-sided speed bounds follow from the coordinate geodesic equation and the differential inequality w′≤‖Γ‖_K w² (with cor-bounded-derivative-implies-lipschitz and thm-ftc-second-part), which the item proves in full. Chrusciel's Proposition 2.2.6 proof contains the same local second-derivative estimate bounding a geodesic by its initial data in a small ball, and Minguzzi's Theorem 2.4 convexity argument is the second independent treatment.

The strict-convexity theorem is authored locally; its convexity kernel is lem-gr-coordinate-ball-geodesic-convexity together with the joint exponential diffeomorphism of thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map. The independent treatments are Minguzzi, Definition 2.3 and Theorem 2.4 (pp. 26-27), and Chrusciel, Sections 2.2-2.3 with Propositions 2.2.3 and 2.2.6 (pp. 10-13).

The construction h′=(1+|df|_h²)h with a proper exhausting f and the completeness of each component are proved in the item; the residual closed-bounded-compact step is the Hopf-Rinow equivalence. Minguzzi, section 1.6 with Theorem 1.5 (pp. 10-11) records the conformal-class completion and the Hopf-Rinow compactness of closed balls, and Lemma 2.17 (pp. 33-34) the unbounded-arclength counterpart; that article is fetch-verified in this coverage file.
